sections.text:
Online safe reinforcement learning (RL) seeks policies that maximize reward while satisfying safety constraints. Reward and safety can induce multimodal action distributions, challenging the prevailing primal-dual methods: Gaussian actors may collapse onto a single suboptimal mode, and optimization over the nonconvex Lagrangian landscape can be unstable.

Diffusion and flow policies can represent such distributions, but recent work with a diffusion actor relies on estimating and matching the score of an augmented-Lagrangian target policy. Instead, we differentiate the augmented objective directly through the generation path of a flow policy, so no score needs to be estimated.

Because a flow policy lacks a readily available action log-density for entropy regularization, we build on the density-free kinetic-energy regularizer of FLAC, a recent reward-only method, and propose Reparameterized Augmented-Lagrangian Flow Actor with Least Energy (RAFALE), an off-policy actor-critic method for safe RL.

We formulate its update as a constrained one-ended generalized Schr\"odinger bridge and show that, for each source draw, this path-space problem is exactly an entropy-regularized problem in action space.

At positive noise, its solution reweights the reward-only action distribution only where the estimated cost exceeds a threshold set by the Lagrange multiplier. As the noise vanishes, the optimal value converges to that of a least-energy map objective that the flow policy optimizes directly.

Across seven Safety-Gymnasium tasks, RAFALE achieves competitive reward with mean final cost within budget on every task, whereas strong baselines trade one for the other; ablations support the necessity of both its augmented objective and its flow actor.

summary.en: The paper introduces RAFALE, an off-policy actor-critic method for safe reinforcement learning with potentially multimodal reward and safety objectives. It differentiates an augmented objective through a flow policy’s generation path, avoiding score estimation, and uses a density-free kinetic-energy regularizer. The authors formulate the update as a constrained one-ended generalized Schrödinger bridge and state that, for each source draw, the path-space problem equals an entropy-regularized action-space problem. Across seven Safety-Gymnasium tasks, they report competitive reward and mean final cost within budget on every task; ablations support the augmented objective and flow actor.
summary.zh: 文章针对安全强化学习中奖励与安全约束可能诱发多峰动作分布、使高斯策略陷入次优模式及原始—对偶优化不稳定的问题，提出 RAFALE，一种离策略演员—评论家方法。它沿流策略的生成路径直接对增广目标求导，无需估计分数，并采用密度无关的动能正则项。作者将更新表述为受约束的单端广义薛定谔桥，并说明其路径空间问题对每个源样本等价于动作空间中的熵正则问题。七项 Safety-Gymnasium 任务中，作者报告其奖励具竞争力且各任务平均最终成本均在预算内；消融实验支持增广目标和流策略的必要性。

items.title: Constrained Flow Policy Updates: A Generalized Schr\"odinger Bridge View

sections.text:
The design of multi-agent robotic systems involves tightly coupled decisions spanning heterogeneous domains, including robot design, fleet composition, and planning. Much effort has been devoted to isolated improvements in these domains, while system-level co-design considering trade-offs and task requirements remains underexplored.

In this work, we present a formal and compositional framework for the task-driven co-design of heterogeneous multi-robot systems, and propose robotic phase diagrams as a qualitative design guideline.

Building on monotone co-design theory, we introduce general abstractions of robots, fleets, planners, executors, and evaluators as interconnected design problems with well-defined interfaces that are agnostic to both implementations and tasks.

This structure enables efficient joint optimization of robot design, fleet composition, and planning under task-specific performance constraints. A series of case studies demonstrates the capabilities of the framework.

New component solutions can be seamlessly incorporated, including robot types, task profiles, and probabilistic sensing objectives, while non-obvious design alternatives are systematically uncovered with optimality guarantees.

The results highlight the flexibility, scalability, and interpretability of the proposed approach, illustrate how formal co-design enables principled reasoning about complex heterogeneous multi-robot systems, and how a robotic phase diagram qualitatively guides the design.

summary.en: The paper presents a task-driven framework for co-designing heterogeneous multi-robot systems, jointly considering robot design, fleet composition, and planning. It also proposes robotic phase diagrams as qualitative design guides. Drawing on monotone co-design theory, the framework models robots, fleets, planners, executors, and evaluators as connected design problems with defined interfaces independent of implementation and task. Case studies demonstrate joint optimization under task-specific performance constraints and incorporation of new robot types, task profiles, and probabilistic sensing objectives. The authors report systematic discovery of non-obvious alternatives with optimality guarantees, and describe the approach as flexible, scalable, and interpretable.
summary.zh: 文章提出面向任务的异构多机器人系统协同设计框架，联合考虑机器人设计、编队组成与规划，并提出机器人相图作为定性设计指南。框架基于单调协同设计理论，将机器人、编队、规划器、执行器和评估器抽象为具有明确定义接口的互联设计问题，接口不依赖具体实现或任务。该结构支持在任务性能约束下进行联合优化。案例研究展示了纳入新机器人类型、任务配置和概率感知目标的能力；作者称框架可系统发现非显然设计方案并提供最优性保证，也强调其灵活性、可扩展性和可解释性。

items.title: Task-Driven Co-Design of Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Systems

sections.text:
Symmetry (or invariance) is a powerful structural property that enables efficient, effective solutions for estimation and control. However, the constraints imposed on a system's dynamics by classical invariance make symmetry a very rigid property, which may be broken by external forces or confined to only a portion of the overall system.

Seeking greater flexibility, this work introduces a novel relaxed notion of symmetry, termed ``weak invariance'', in which the non-symmetric part of the dynamics (the ``residual'') can be captured entirely by another control system evolving on the symmetry group.

Weakly invariant systems are strictly more general than classical invariant systems, but they nonetheless enjoy many similar favorable properties.

In particular, we prove that any weakly invariant system admits a cascade decomposition in which the driven subsystem is group affine, showing that weak symmetry generalizes not only classical symmetry, but also the (thus far distinct) class of group affine systems.

We also show that a weak symmetry with autonomous residual can be factored out of the system's error dynamics, enabling yet a greater reduction of dimensionality as compared to classical symmetries.

Finally, we study the example of an aerial vehicle under the influence of gravity, for which we propose a nine-dimensional weak symmetry (strictly containing the system's familiar four-dimensional classical symmetry).

Weak invariance thus generalizes classical symmetry while also preserving key structural properties, thereby laying a foundation for more flexible methods of symmetry-informed control.

summary.en: The paper introduces weak invariance for control systems, allowing nonsymmetric dynamics to be represented by a residual control system evolving on a symmetry group. The authors prove that weakly invariant systems generalize classical invariant systems and admit a cascade decomposition with a group-affine driven subsystem. When the residual is autonomous, the weak symmetry can be factored out of the error dynamics. An aerial vehicle under gravity illustrates the proposal, with a nine-dimensional weak symmetry containing its familiar four-dimensional classical symmetry.
summary.zh: 论文提出控制系统的“弱不变性”：系统动力学中的非对称残差可由另一个在对称群上演化的控制系统完整描述。作者证明，弱不变系统比经典不变系统更一般，并具有若干相似结构性质；它可分解为级联系统，其中受驱子系统为群仿射系统。若残差自治，弱对称性还可从误差动力学中约去。作者以受重力影响的飞行器为例，提出一种包含其经典四维对称性的九维弱对称性。

items.title: A Weak Notion of Symmetry for Control Systems

sections.text:
Language models trained on large-scale vision-language data have demonstrated strong potential for embodied agents. Harnessing models through embodied tools use offers a promising alternative to end-to-end vision-language-action systems by combining high-level reasoning with external modules for perception, planning, and control.

However, it remains unclear what makes an effective harness for embodied manipulation, and to what extent such a harness can unlock embodied capabilities in a wide range of reasoning models.

In this work, we present Guava, a harness framework for embodied tool use developed through systematic exploration of the design space of agent workflows, action spaces, and observation spaces.

Our study identifies three key ingredients for effective embodied agents: iterative perception-reasoning-action loops, semantic action abstractions, and multimodal observations.

To understand whether these design principles are universal even to small models, we develop an end-to-end training pipeline that distills embodied manipulation capabilities into a 4B open-source model using fewer than 2K trajectories collected entirely in simulation.

Experimental results in both simulation and real-world environments show performance comparable to frontier proprietary models while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen objects, novel instructions, and long-horizon tasks.

Results suggest that a well-designed harness can serve as a scalable, model-agnostic interface for embodied manipulation, enabling strong emergent embodied capabilities in compact open-source models with minimal training data.

summary.en: The paper presents Guava, a harness framework for embodied manipulation developed by exploring agent workflows, action spaces, and observation spaces. It identifies iterative perception-reasoning-action loops, semantic action abstractions, and multimodal observations as key ingredients. The authors train a 4B open-source model through an end-to-end pipeline using fewer than 2,000 trajectories collected entirely in simulation. Experiments in simulation and real-world environments report performance comparable to frontier proprietary models, with generalization to unseen objects, novel instructions, and long-horizon tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于具身操作的 Guava 工具框架，通过系统探索智能体工作流、动作空间和观测空间来设计具身工具使用。研究指出，有效框架包含迭代的感知—推理—行动循环、语义化动作抽象和多模态观测。作者还用完全在仿真中收集的少于两千条轨迹，将操作能力蒸馏到一个 4B 开源模型。仿真和真实环境实验显示，该模型表现可比专有前沿模型，并能泛化至未见物体、新指令和长时任务。

items.title: Guava: Distilling Frontier VLM Agents into a Compact Model with a Manipulation Harness

Compositional generalization recombines skills to solve new tasks, and skill generalization lets the learned policy behind each skill work in new situations. sections.text:
Robots that learn from a few demonstrations often require two forms of generalization. Compositional generalization recombines skills to solve new tasks, and skill generalization lets the learned policy behind each skill work in new situations. The two depend on each other, yet information is lost between composition and the skills it calls.

Where a skill works is determined by the structure its policy is trained with, while composition sees the skill only through a separate description, such as a name, an instruction, or a symbolic operator, that omits this structure. Our key idea is to use each policy's structural prior as part of the interface between composition and the skill.

A structural prior states what a behavior depends on, for example that a grasp depends only on the gripper's pose relative to the object. Built into training, it shapes where the policy generalizes; stated in language, it tells composition where the policy applies. We instantiate this idea in Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning (APPL).

A construction agent segments complete demonstrations into reusable skills, proposes several structural priors for each skill, and trains and verifies one policy per prior. A runtime agent then selects among these prior-specific policies and composes them toward new task goals using their interfaces.

Across MetaWorld and long-horizon ManiSkill tasks, APPL improves out-of-distribution skill generalization and enables previously unseen skill compositions; ablating the interface information substantially reduces performance. These results support the use of training-time structural assumptions as a bridge between skill learning and skill composition.

summary.en: The paper proposes Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning (APPL), using structural priors of skill policies both to shape training and to inform the interface for skill composition. A construction agent segments demonstrations, proposes priors, and trains and verifies a policy for each; a runtime agent selects and composes these policies for new goals. Evaluations on MetaWorld and long-horizon ManiSkill tasks report improved out-of-distribution skill generalization and previously unseen compositions. Ablations show substantially lower performance when interface information is removed.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning（APPL），将技能策略的结构先验同时用于策略训练和技能组合接口。构建智能体把演示切分为可复用技能，为每项技能提出多个先验，并据此训练和验证策略；运行时智能体根据这些接口选择策略、组合技能以实现新目标。作者在 MetaWorld 和长时程 ManiSkill 任务上的评估显示，APPL 改善了分布外技能泛化，并支持此前未见的技能组合；消融结果显示，去除接口信息会显著降低表现。

items.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning

sections.text:
Manual dense annotation remains a major obstacle to deploying semantic segmentation models in new driving environments. Active domain adaptation (ADA) seeks label-efficient transfer by annotating only a selected portion of the target domain.

Existing ADA methods commonly implement this process through multiple rounds of acquisition, annotation, and retraining. We study a practical one-shot image-level setting that selects and densely annotates a fixed target subset in a single round, followed by uninterrupted adaptation.

Within this setting, we develop Target-Calibrated Active Domain Adaptation (TC-ADA) as a joint design of complete-image acquisition and target-calibrated adaptation.

Stage~1 uses visual representations from a vision foundation model (VFM) together with semantic predictions from a fixed unsupervised domain adaptation model to select representative and informative target images without target annotations.

Stage~2 jointly uses labeled source data, labeled target data, and the remaining unlabeled target data, while calibrating source and target supervision under limited target labels. Extensive experiments across five synthetic-to-real and real-to-real driving transfers show consistent improvements over representative ADA baselines.

With only 23 to 46 labeled target images on four transfers and 140 on Mapillary, TC-ADA stays within 1.9 mean intersection over union (mIoU) points of target-only full supervision. Code will be available at https://github.com/ywher/TC-ADA.

summary.en: The paper studies one-shot, image-level active domain adaptation for driving-scene semantic segmentation and proposes TC-ADA, combining complete-image selection with target-calibrated adaptation. Its first stage selects representative, informative target images without target labels, using visual foundation model representations and predictions from a fixed unsupervised adaptation model. The second stage uses labeled source and target data together with unlabeled target data, calibrating supervision across domains. Experiments across five synthetic-to-real and real-to-real transfers report consistent gains over representative baselines; under the stated label budgets, performance is within 1.9 mIoU points of target-only full supervision.
summary.zh: 论文研究驾驶场景语义分割中的单轮图像级主动域适应，并提出 TC-ADA，将完整图像筛选与目标域校准适应联合设计。第一阶段结合视觉基础模型表征和固定无监督域适应模型的语义预测，在无目标标注时选择具有代表性且信息丰富的目标图像；第二阶段联合利用有标签源数据、有标签目标数据和未标注目标数据，并校准两域监督。五种合成到真实及真实到真实迁移实验显示，相比代表性基线有稳定提升；在所述标注量下，结果与目标域全监督相差不超过 1.9 个 mIoU 点。

items.title: TC-ADA: One-Shot Active Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation

Recent works tackle this with learning-based models trained at scale and with approaches built on vision-language models (VLMs). sections.text:
Safe and robust robot navigation across diverse environments requires a high-level understanding of complex scenes and the ability to carry it into stable motion. Recent works tackle this with learning-based models trained at scale and with approaches built on vision-language models (VLMs).

However, learning-based models break down outside their training distribution, while VLM-based approaches bring that understanding but rarely ground it in the scene or align the action with it.

To address these limitations, we present RECAST, a robot navigation framework that combines the reasoning of a VLM with the spatial grounding of vision foundation models to build an Actionable Cost map.

Given the robot's front view and the user's instruction, we first decompose the scene with the VLM, judging which surfaces are traversable, which objects pose a risk, which heading to prefer, and which gaps are passable.

Vision foundation models then ground these surfaces and objects in the image, and all four judgments are spatially recast into one compact cost map. This map both conditions the trajectory decoders and scores their proposals to select the one to execute.

As the VLM's answers trail the live scene, both steps draw on cost maps from two points in time: the pivot frame the VLM judged, which carries all four judgments, and the current frame, whose terrain and collision costs are rebuilt from the current image.

RECAST improves success over the strongest prior method by 13.3 points in simulation and 31.4 points on a real quadruped, and reduces the collision rate relative to it by 9.6 and 14.3 points, reaching the lowest collision rate among all methods. The project page is available at https://recast-nav.github.io/

summary.en: RECAST combines scene reasoning from a vision-language model with spatial grounding from vision foundation models. Given a robot’s forward view and a user instruction, it assesses traversable surfaces, risks, preferred heading, and passable gaps, then consolidates them into an actionable cost map for trajectory decoding and proposal scoring. To account for delayed VLM judgments, it uses both the judged pivot-frame map and terrain and collision costs rebuilt from the current image. The authors report higher success and lower collision rates than the strongest prior method in simulation and on a real quadruped.
summary.zh: RECAST结合视觉语言模型的场景推理与视觉基础模型的空间定位，根据机器人前视图和用户指令判断可通行表面、风险物体、偏好方向及可通过间隙，并将判断整合为可执行代价图，用于轨迹解码和候选评分。为应对模型判断滞后，框架同时利用判断帧代价图与依据当前图像更新的地形和碰撞代价。作者报告，相较最强既有方法，仿真成功率提高13.3个百分点，真实四足机器人上提高31.4个百分点，碰撞率分别降低9.6和14.3个百分点。

items.title: RECAST: Recasting Vision-Language Semantics into an Actionable Cost Map for Robot Navigation

sections.text:
Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) threats have emerged as a defining security challenge of the 21st century.

This paper presents DroneShield-AI, a unified open framework integrating six processing layers: RF signal classification, acoustic motor-signature detection, YOLOv8-based visual detection, evidence-weighted sensor fusion, a Behavioral Intent Classification Engine (BICE), and a Graph Neural Network Swarm Intelligence Module (GNN-SIM).

This v2 revision reports measured results on the completed implementation (495 automated tests), superseding the v1 simulation-only preprint.

On real public data: RF presence detection reaches F1 0.9924; acoustic detection reaches 98.12% accuracy, though a 4-feature statistical baseline reaches 93.25% on the same split, so the model's drone-specific contribution is approximately 4.9 points, a property of dataset provenance rather than a leakage bug; visual detection (YOLOv8) reaches AP50 0.8782 on a held-out test split, from a model still improving when training stopped.

No fused-accuracy figure is reportable, since the three real-data layers use independently collected, unsynchronized datasets with no shared ground truth.

BICE and GNN-SIM remain evaluated on physics-calibrated simulation data pending real adversarial and swarm field data: BICE shows a consistent robustness advantage over a trivial baseline under distribution shift; GNN-SIM underperforms its own trivial baseline in-distribution but independently replicates BICE's noise-robustness advantage, regarded as this work's most durable finding.

All code, trained checkpoints, and the full test suite are publicly released.

summary.en: DroneShield-AI integrates radio-frequency classification, acoustic detection, YOLOv8 visual detection, evidence-weighted fusion, behavioral intent classification, and a swarm-intelligence module. The revision reports results from a completed implementation and 495 automated tests. On public real-world data, RF detection reaches an F1 of 0.9924, acoustic accuracy is 98.12% against a 93.25% statistical baseline, and visual detection reaches AP50 0.8782. Because the three real-data layers use independently collected, unsynchronized datasets, no fused accuracy is reported. The intent and swarm modules are evaluated only on physics-calibrated simulation data; the swarm module trails its trivial baseline in-distribution.
summary.zh: DroneShield-AI是整合射频分类、声学检测、YOLOv8视觉检测、证据加权融合、行为意图分类和群体智能模块的开源框架。修订版报告了已完成实现及495项自动化测试结果：在真实公开数据上，射频检测F1为0.9924，声学准确率为98.12%，视觉检测AP50为0.8782；声学统计基线已达93.25%。由于三类真实数据集独立采集且不同步，作者不报告融合准确率。行为意图和群体智能模块仅在经物理校准的仿真数据上评估，后者在分布内表现低于简单基线。

sections.text:
Rearranging objects in cluttered tabletop environments remains a long-standing challenge in robotics. Classical planners often generate inefficient, high-cost plans by moving objects individually and using fixed buffers, temporary spaces such as unoccupied tabletop regions or static stacks, to resolve conflicts.

When only free tabletop locations are used as buffers, planning in dense scenes becomes difficult, since placing an object can prevent others from reaching their goals and complicate subsequent planning.

Stacking provides additional buffer capacity, but conventional stacking is static: the base object cannot be relocated while holding another, which limits efficiency. To address these limitations, a novel planning primitive called the Dynamic Buffer is introduced.

Inspired by human grouping strategies, it enables robots to form temporary, movable stacks that can be transported as a unit. Dynamic buffers improve feasibility and efficiency in dense layouts and reduce travel in large-scale scenarios where buffer space is ample.

Compared with a state-of-the-art rearrangement planner, the proposed approach reduces total manipulator travel cost by 13.48% in dense stationary-manipulator scenarios and by 4.34% in large-scale, low-density scenarios involving mobile manipulators. Practicality is validated through execution on a Delta robot with a parallel-jaw gripper.

These results establish dynamic buffering as a key primitive for cost-efficient and robust rearrangement planning.

summary.en: The paper introduces Dynamic Buffers, a planning primitive that lets robots form temporary movable stacks and transport them as a unit. The method is intended to address the limited capacity and access conflicts of fixed buffers in cluttered tabletop rearrangement. Compared with a state-of-the-art rearrangement planner, it reduces total manipulator travel cost by 13.48% in dense scenarios with a stationary manipulator and by 4.34% in large, low-density scenarios with mobile manipulators. The authors also validate practical execution on a Delta robot equipped with a parallel-jaw gripper.
summary.zh: 论文提出动态缓冲规划原语，使机器人能够组成可移动的临时堆叠，并将其作为整体搬运，以缓解密集桌面重排中固定缓冲区容量有限、物体互相阻挡的问题。作者报告，与先进重排规划器相比，该方法在操纵器固定的密集场景中将总移动成本降低13.48%，在低密度、大规模移动操纵器场景中降低4.34%。研究还通过带平行夹爪的Delta机器人执行验证其实用性。

items.title: Dynamic Buffers: Cost-Efficient Planning for Tabletop Rearrangement with Stacking

We introduce CausalDriveBench, an evaluation framework grounded in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy (PCH) that tests causal reasoning in driving-specific VLAs through structured visual question answering (QA) and alternative-trajectory prediction. To this end, we construct causal scene graphs over nuScenes that distinguish causally active, dormant, and distractor entities, separating perceptual

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for autonomous driving produce natural-language reasoning alongside predicted trajectories, but whether this reasoning reflects the causal structure of the scene remains untested.

We introduce CausalDriveBench, an evaluation framework grounded in Pearl's Causal Hierarchy (PCH) that tests causal reasoning in driving-specific VLAs through structured visual question answering (QA) and alternative-trajectory prediction.

To this end, we construct causal scene graphs over nuScenes that distinguish causally active, dormant, and distractor entities, separating perceptual salience from causal relevance. The benchmark spans all four rungs of PCH (association, intervention, and counterfactual along with causal discovery) for QA generation.

For the higher rungs, we additionally provide reference trajectories under specified scene modifications, enabling action-level verification that complements reasoning-level evaluation. In total, the benchmark contains 7,285 verified causal QA pairs and 1,000 counterfactual trajectories derived from nuScenes.

We evaluate 10 driving-specific VLAs and 3 general-purpose VLMs, and report three findings. First, the best model reaches only 70.6% QA accuracy, and 4 of 13 models score below random chance.

Second, comparing each driving VLA to the general-purpose VLM that shares its language backbone, the cost of driving fine-tuning ranges from 2 to 34 percentage points on causal QA, with post-training design explaining the spread.

Third, causal QA and trajectory accuracy are statistically uncorrelated across models: under counterfactual prompts, predicted trajectories either over-react or collapse onto the observed-scene baseline. Taken together, these results show that neither fluent rationales nor accurate observed-scene trajectories constitute evidence of causal understanding.

summary.en: CausalDriveBench evaluates causal reasoning in autonomous-driving vision-language-action models using scene graphs that distinguish causally active, dormant, and distracting entities in nuScenes. It includes 7,285 verified causal question-answer pairs and 1,000 counterfactual trajectories, and was used to assess 10 driving-specific VLAs and three general-purpose VLMs. The authors report that the best QA accuracy is 70.6%, while causal QA and trajectory accuracy are statistically uncorrelated across models. Under counterfactual prompts, predicted trajectories either overreact or collapse to the observed-scene baseline.
summary.zh: CausalDriveBench用于评估自动驾驶视觉语言行动模型的因果推理，基于nuScenes构建区分因果活跃、休眠与干扰实体的场景图，并涵盖因果层级各阶段的问答及反事实轨迹预测。基准包含7,285组经验证的因果问答和1,000条反事实轨迹；研究评估了10个驾驶专用模型和3个通用视觉语言模型。作者报告，最佳问答准确率为70.6%，且跨模型因果问答与轨迹准确率无统计相关；反事实提示下，轨迹预测会过度反应或退回观测场景基线。

items.title: CausalDriveBench: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving

The resulting inference latency makes it difficult for robots to respond quickly, especially in dynamic environments. sections.text:
Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models are highly effective for generalist robot manipulation, yet their reliance on computationally expensive VLM encoding and multi-step iterative action generation imposes a significant latency bottleneck.

The resulting inference latency makes it difficult for robots to respond quickly, especially in dynamic environments. We address this limitation with RAVEL (Rolling Asynchronous VLA Enabling Low-Latency Control), an asynchronous inference framework that addresses the computational bottlenecks of both the VLM backbone and the action expert.

To reduce the delay from multi-step action denoising, RAVEL allows near-term actions to be executed after a single denoising step by carrying partially denoised future actions forward in a rolling buffer.

To avoid blocking on slow VLM encoding, RAVEL decouples VLM encoding from rolling action generation, allowing the action expert to operate continuously using the latest available VLM context, while a lightweight Fast Observation Pathway (FOP) directly conditions the action expert on current observations.

Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, RAVEL consistently achieves substantially lower response latency while maintaining the task capability of the underlying VLA, enabling high-frequency and responsive closed-loop control.

summary.en: The paper introduces RAVEL, an asynchronous inference framework for flow-based vision-language-action models, targeting latency from visual-language encoding and iterative action generation. It decouples encoding from rolling action generation, lets the action expert use the latest available context, and adds a Fast Observation Pathway for current observations. A rolling buffer carries partially denoised future actions forward so near-term actions can be executed after one denoising step. The authors report lower response latency while maintaining the underlying model’s task capability across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RAVEL，一种面向流式视觉—语言—动作模型的异步推理框架，旨在缓解视觉语言模型编码和多步动作生成带来的延迟。它将视觉语言编码与滚动动作生成解耦，使动作专家使用最新可用上下文持续运行，并通过快速观测通路直接利用当前观测；滚动缓冲区则保留部分去噪的未来动作，使近期动作经单步去噪后即可执行。作者报告，在仿真和真实操作任务中，该方法降低了响应延迟，同时保持底层模型的任务能力。

items.title: RAVEL: Asynchronous Rolling Inference for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

These domains offer scarce training data and only onboard compute, yet deployed systems must face novelty without erasing prior competence. sections.text:
Unattended interactive autonomy - machines that step into danger in place of humans and complete tasks with human tools - remains a missing capability in mission-critical operations. These domains offer scarce training data and only onboard compute, yet deployed systems must face novelty without erasing prior competence.

We introduce Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs), which learn efficiently in the lab and continue learning after deployment through autonomous, gradient-free, on-device updates. CFAM uses a complementary learning architecture with a frozen slow-learning component and a fast-learning Capsule Field.

The slow component contains three cortices: Sensor, which maps multimodal input into 3D-grounded geometry; Reasoning, which decomposes tasks into skills and evaluates outcomes; and Action, which executes geometric skills. The Capsule Field stores field learning one-shot and gradient-free as Competence Capsules.

Skill installation is few-shot in the lab and continual in the field; open-world novelty is outside scope. We evaluate CFAM across five embodiments: manipulator, quadruped, humanoid, quadrotor, and off-road vehicle. Baselines (pi0, CogACT, SpatialVLA) use the same in-house multi-embodiment dataset for physical-platform comparisons.

CFAM reaches the operating point of a standard policy trained on the full prior-training dataset using 40% of the data, or 2.5x fewer trajectories. At test time, autonomous capture of verified near-OOD cases improves action success by 13.9 percentage points. In sequential simulation, backward transfer is -0.5 percentage points versus -11.4 for LoRA.

CFAM therefore provides a bounded form of post-deployment physical intelligence: few-shot skill learning, autonomous field growth from verified near-OOD experience, and retention of prior competence.

summary.en: The paper presents Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for post-deployment physical AI. CFAM combines a frozen slow-learning component, with Sensor, Reasoning, and Action cortices, and a fast Capsule Field that stores learning as gradient-free Competence Capsules. Skills are installed few-shot in the lab, while verified near-OOD experience can be captured autonomously in the field; open-world novelty is outside scope. Evaluations cover five embodiments. The authors report reaching a full-data standard policy’s operating point with 40% of the data and a 13.9 percentage-point action-success improvement from autonomous capture of verified near-OOD cases.
summary.zh: 论文提出持续现场自适应模型 CFAM，面向部署后的物理智能系统，采用冻结的慢学习组件与快速学习的 Capsule Field，通过无梯度设备端更新持续积累能力。慢组件包含感知、推理和动作模块；技能可在实验室通过少样本安装，现场则以能力胶囊记录学习。作者在五类机器人形态上评估，并称使用全部先前训练数据的 40% 即达到标准策略的运行水平；对经验证的近分布外案例进行自主捕获后，动作成功率提高 13.9 个百分点。新颖开放世界情形不在研究范围内。

items.title: Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for Post-Deployment Physical AI

In this context, robots are a key technology for facilitating the construction of future human outposts. Toward the deployment and establishment of human habitation modules on the lunar surface, we propose a combined system consisting of inflatable modules and a modular, reconfigurable robotic system. This paper presents a report demonstrating various robot-assisted task executions using real hardware

sections.text:
Long-term human habitation and in-situ development on the Moon open a new era of space utilization. In this context, robots are a key technology for facilitating the construction of future human outposts.

Toward the deployment and establishment of human habitation modules on the lunar surface, we propose a combined system consisting of inflatable modules and a modular, reconfigurable robotic system.

This paper presents a report demonstrating various robot-assisted task executions using real hardware, namely the modular and reconfigurable robot MoonBot and the inflatable module HIDAS, to enhance the reliability of their deployment and maintenance.

The demonstrated tasks include robotic inspection during inflation, module position alignment, final safety locking, and three-dimensional mapping for post-deployment maintenance. All demonstrations were conducted either in a laboratory environment or at a lunar analogue test site.

Finally, lessons learned are discussed to provide essential insights for this robotic application to future lunar habitation.

summary.en: The paper reports hardware demonstrations of robot-assisted deployment and maintenance for inflatable habitation modules, using the reconfigurable MoonBot robot and HIDAS module. Demonstrated tasks include inspection during inflation, module alignment, final safety locking, and three-dimensional mapping for post-deployment maintenance. All demonstrations took place in a laboratory or at a lunar analogue test site. The authors also discuss lessons learned for applying this robotic system to future lunar habitation.
summary.zh: 论文报告了机器人辅助部署和维护月球充气居住舱的实物演示，系统由可重构模块化机器人 MoonBot 和充气模块 HIDAS 组成。展示任务包括充气过程中的机器人检查、舱体位置对准、最终安全锁定，以及部署后的三维测绘维护。所有演示均在实验室或月球类比测试场地进行，并讨论了相关经验，为未来月球居住设施应用提供参考。

items.title: Robot-Assisted Deployment and Maintenance of Inflatable Modules for Lunar Habitation: A Field Demonstration

sections.text:
Language-conditioned robot policies have made clear progress in multitask manipulation, but task-relevant local visual evidence usually stays hidden inside a visual backbone or attention layers. This leaves the policy difficult to inspect and fragile under visual change, two symptoms of a missing explicit, task-aligned local visual channel.

We present TLC-DiT, a plug-in extension of the Multitask Diffusion Transformer (DiT) policy that adds explicit task-guided local visual feature maps without changing the diffusion objective or the action-generation process.

For each camera view, frozen DINOv2 patch features are modulated by the CLIP task embedding through FiLM and refined by a lightweight CoordConv CNN adapter into smooth spatial maps, which are concatenated with the original global image, language, joint-state, and timestep conditions.

On LIBERO, TLC-DiT reaches a 93.5% average success rate, compared with 86.5% for Multitask DiT and 79.25% for SmolVLA. On LIBERO-plus, the total success rate improves from 54.07% to 57.24%, with larger gains under camera, background, and sensor-noise changes.

In real-world bimanual tasks, TLC-DiT raises Teabag Putting completion from 44% to 89% while maintaining comparable Match Box Opening performance. Feature-map visualizations confirm that the model attends to task-relevant regions across views and perturbations, providing a direct way to inspect the visual evidence.

summary.en: The paper introduces TLC-DiT, a plug-in extension to a Multitask Diffusion Transformer policy that adds explicit task-guided local visual feature maps without changing the diffusion objective or action-generation process. CLIP task embeddings modulate frozen DINOv2 patch features, which a lightweight adapter refines into spatial maps. The authors report improved success rates on LIBERO, LIBERO-plus, and real-world bimanual tasks, with gains under visual perturbations. Feature-map visualizations indicate attention to task-relevant regions across views and perturbations.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TLC-DiT，作为多任务扩散 Transformer 策略的插件式扩展，加入显式、任务引导的局部视觉特征图，不改变扩散目标或动作生成过程。方法以 CLIP 任务嵌入调制冻结的 DINOv2 图像块特征，再经轻量适配器生成空间图，并与原有条件拼接。作者报告，该方法在 LIBERO、LIBERO-plus 及真实双臂任务中取得成功率提升，尤其在视觉扰动下有所改善；特征图可视化显示模型关注任务相关区域。

items.title: TLC-DiT: Task-Aligned Local Visual Conditioning for Robust Multitask Robot Manipulation

We present MonoEgo, a capture system that replaces active wrist instrumentation with offline monocular reconstruction. One 90-FPS global-shutter camera observes calibrated passive wrist constellations, sparse workstation anchors, and the scene on a shared image clock. MonoTag SLAM combines marker corners with ORB geometry and uses visual evidence to reject ambiguous planar-marker poses. Its metric Atlas supports interval scale re-anchoring, verified map

sections.text:
Image-aligned metric demonstrations often require dedicated tracking hardware and synchronization across devices. We present MonoEgo, a capture system that replaces active wrist instrumentation with offline monocular reconstruction.

One 90-FPS global-shutter camera observes calibrated passive wrist constellations, sparse workstation anchors, and the scene on a shared image clock. MonoTag SLAM combines marker corners with ORB geometry and uses visual evidence to reject ambiguous planar-marker poses.

Its metric Atlas supports interval scale re-anchoring, verified map merging, and retrospective localization of earlier frames supported by the final map. Camera and wrist-constellation outputs retain validity and map provenance, and unsupported motion is left missing.

Experiments show metric tracking beyond continuous anchor visibility, reconnection of supported map components, and recovery of some missing camera poses.

Comparisons against a multisensor camera reference and separate stationary-constellation tests characterize trajectory agreement and precision while revealing incomplete coverage and residual geometric uncertainty. The results indicate that passive fixtures and offline reconstruction can reduce capture-side requirements.

Dynamic accuracy, deployment, and downstream policy benefits require further study.

summary.en: MonoEgo uses one global-shutter camera and passive wrist markers with sparse workstation anchors to capture metric demonstrations through offline monocular reconstruction. MonoTag SLAM combines marker corners and ORB geometry, rejecting ambiguous planar poses. The system supports scale re-anchoring, map merging, and retrospective localization while recording validity and map provenance; unsupported motion remains missing. Experiments report tracking beyond continuous anchor visibility and recovery of some poses, while comparisons also show incomplete coverage and residual geometric uncertainty. Dynamic accuracy, deployment, and downstream policy benefits remain to be studied.
summary.zh: MonoEgo 使用单台全局快门相机观测被动腕部标记、工作台锚点和场景，通过离线单目重建生成带尺度的演示轨迹。MonoTag SLAM 结合标记角点与 ORB 几何信息，并拒绝含糊的平面标记位姿；系统还支持尺度重锚定、地图合并及基于最终地图回溯定位，且保留数据有效性和地图来源，不支持的运动留空。实验显示其可在锚点不可见时持续跟踪、连接受支持的地图组件并恢复部分缺失位姿；与多传感器参考及静态标记测试的比较也显示覆盖不完整和几何不确定性。动态精度、部署及下游策略收益仍待研究。

items.title: MonoEgo: Monocular Metric Egocentric Demonstration Capture with Passive Wrist Constellations and Sparse Workstation Anchors

Latent-space reinforcement learning avoids updating the pretrained generator by controlling its initial sampling noise, yet high-dimensional noise can have strongly anisotropic effects on decoded actions. Soft Actor-Critic controls the leading response directions, while

sections.text:
Generative robot policies provide expressive behavior priors, but updating a large diffusion or flow-matching model through online interaction is costly. Latent-space reinforcement learning avoids updating the pretrained generator by controlling its initial sampling noise, yet high-dimensional noise can have strongly anisotropic effects on decoded actions.

We introduce Principal Steering Subspaces (PSS), a forward-query interface that constructs a fixed low-dimensional control basis from finite-difference decoder responses. Soft Actor-Critic controls the leading response directions, while the orthogonal complement is independently resampled from the Gaussian prior at each query.

On three RoboMimic tasks with diffusion and flow-matching policies, response spectra reveal substantial concentration. Across five matched task-generator pairs, the training curves indicate that PSS generally converges faster and exhibits more stable late-training behavior than full-latent control, while achieving stronger final performance overall.

Controlled Diffusion-Square ablations further show that leading-response directions outperform random and least-responsive subspaces of equal dimension.

We further integrate PSS with a frozen, closed-source 3B-parameter vision-language-action (VLA) policy in a humanoid learning system with synchronous transition collection, reset-time optimization, and latency-aware asynchronous deployment.

In an exploratory screwdriver-placement evaluation, success is observed in 2/10 trials for the frozen VLA policy and 6/10 after SAC+PSS adaptation. These results support decoder-response geometry as a practical basis for online adaptation of frozen generative robot policies.

summary.en: Principal Steering Subspaces (PSS) builds a fixed low-dimensional control basis from finite-difference decoder responses. Soft Actor-Critic controls leading directions, while the orthogonal complement is resampled from a Gaussian prior at each query. On three RoboMimic tasks using diffusion and flow-matching policies, the authors report concentrated response spectra and generally faster convergence, more stable late training, and stronger overall final performance than full-latent control across five matched pairs. Ablations favor leading-response over equal-dimensional random or least-responsive subspaces. In an exploratory screwdriver-placement evaluation, success was 2/10 for a frozen VLA policy and 6/10 after adaptation.
summary.zh: Principal Steering Subspaces（PSS）从生成式机器人策略解码器的有限差分响应构造固定低维控制基，由软演员评论家控制主要响应方向，并在每次查询时从高斯先验重采样正交补空间。在三个 RoboMimic 任务及扩散、流匹配策略上，作者报告响应集中；五组匹配比较中，PSS 通常收敛更快、后期更稳定，整体最终表现更强。消融显示主要响应方向优于同维随机或低响应子空间。探索性螺丝刀放置实验中，冻结 VLA 策略成功率为 2/10，适配后为 6/10。

items.title: Principal Steering Subspaces for Online Adaptation of Frozen Generative Robot Policies

items.intro: arXiv:2609.34300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models offer a powerful substrate for safety reasoning in high-dimensional robotic systems, but they are also fallible: their predictions can be biased, miscalibrated, or confidently wrong. This creates a central challenge for latent-space safety filters, which often learn Hamilton-Jacobi safety value functions on the dynamics of a world model. If the world model is incorrect, the resulting value function can inherit its errors and produce overconfident safety estimates. Existing latent safety filters

sections.text:
World models offer a powerful substrate for safety reasoning in high-dimensional robotic systems, but they are also fallible: their predictions can be biased, miscalibrated, or confidently wrong. This creates a central challenge for latent-space safety filters, which often learn Hamilton-Jacobi safety value functions on the dynamics of a world model.

If the world model is incorrect, the resulting value function can inherit its errors and produce overconfident safety estimates.

Existing latent safety filters often rely on auxiliary signals such as ensemble disagreement or value-target consistency residuals for adaptation, but these signals can remain small even when the world model's predictions deviate from observations.

We propose an adaptive latent safety filter that calibrates safety reasoning using directly observed world-model error.

Our method uses Adaptive Conformal Inference to construct online uncertainty sets from discrepancies between predicted and observation-inferred latent states, then evaluates safety pessimistically by minimizing the learned value function over these sets.

This allows the filter to remain minimally conservative when the world model is accurate, while becoming more cautious when observations reveal model mismatch. We provide a finite-time coverage guarantee for the adaptive uncertainty radius.

Through simulation and hardware experiments, we show that our method significantly reduces failures relative to state-of-the-art latent safety filters while preserving task completion.

summary.en: The paper proposes an adaptive latent safety filter for errors that arise when world-model predictions are biased or miscalibrated. Adaptive Conformal Inference constructs online uncertainty sets from discrepancies between predicted and observation-inferred latent states; safety is assessed pessimistically by minimizing the learned value function over each set. The authors provide a finite-time coverage guarantee for the uncertainty radius. The filter is intended to remain minimally conservative when the model is accurate and become more cautious when observations indicate mismatch. In simulation and hardware experiments, the authors report fewer failures than with state-of-the-art latent safety filters while preserving task completion.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种自适应潜空间安全过滤器，针对世界模型偏差导致安全价值函数继承错误、产生过度自信估计的问题。方法使用自适应保形推断，根据预测潜状态与观测推断潜状态之间的差异在线构造不确定集合，并在集合内对学习到的价值函数取保守最小值；作者给出不确定半径的有限时间覆盖保证。模型准确时过滤器可保持较低保守性，观测显示不匹配时则更加谨慎。仿真和硬件实验中，作者报告相较先进潜空间安全过滤器显著减少失败，同时保留任务完成能力。

items.title: When World Models Lie: Adaptive Safety Analysis Under Wrong Imaginations

items.intro: arXiv:2609.35311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Action-conditioned video world models predict future robot interactions from multiple cameras, yet their outputs remain disparate video collections rather than a shared metric scene queryable across viewpoints and time. sections.text:
Action-conditioned video world models predict future robot interactions from multiple cameras, yet their outputs remain disparate video collections rather than a shared metric scene queryable across viewpoints and time.

While existing 4D reconstruction methods offer a path to spatialize these predictions, independently reconstructing and merging each camera stream fails to enforce cross-view consistency. This limitation is particularly detrimental when combining moving robot-mounted cameras with fixed external views.

To address this, we introduce RoGSW4RLD, a feed-forward framework that lifts synchronized multi-camera rollouts into a unified, time-queryable metric 4D Gaussian field. Rather than learning a separate geometric transition model, RoGSW4RLD directly reconstructs the visual future generated by existing world models.

Its core innovation is a two-stage architecture: Stage 1 jointly forms the metric 4D field by fusing cross-view evidence with robot-specific articulated geometry and kinematics, while Stage 2 refines the field's geometry and appearance while strictly preserving the initial temporal displacements.

Evaluated on 256 held-out DROID episodes, RoGSW4RLD significantly outperforms camera-wise reconstruction with calibrated merging, improving novel-view PSNR by 2.15 dB, reducing depth AbsRel by 47%, and lowering robot displacement error by 61%.

These robust gains extend to action-conditioned Cosmos 3 rollouts, demonstrating that predicted video futures can be successfully translated into consistent, spatially queryable 4D metric representations.

summary.en: RoGSW4RLD lifts synchronized multi-camera, action-conditioned video rollouts into a unified metric 4D Gaussian field that can be queried across time and viewpoints. Its two-stage method first fuses cross-view evidence with articulated robot geometry and kinematics, then refines geometry and appearance while preserving initial temporal displacements. It reconstructs visual futures from existing world models rather than learning a separate geometric transition model. On 256 held-out DROID episodes, the authors report improved novel-view PSNR and lower depth and robot-displacement errors than camera-wise reconstruction with calibrated merging. They also report gains on action-conditioned Cosmos 3 rollouts.
summary.zh: RoGSW4RLD 将同步多相机动作条件视频世界模型输出提升为统一、可按时间查询的度量 4D 高斯场。其两阶段框架先融合跨视角证据及机器人关节几何与运动学，再细化几何和外观，同时严格保留初始时间位移；方法直接重建既有世界模型生成的视觉未来，不另学几何转移模型。在 256 个留出 DROID 片段上，相较逐相机重建与标定合并，作者报告新视角 PSNR 提高 2.15 dB、深度 AbsRel 降低 47%、机器人位移误差降低 61%。结果也扩展至动作条件 Cosmos 3 推演。

items.title: RoGSW4RLD: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Lifting for Robot World Model Rollouts

sections.text:
Large language models (LLMs) are now the default cognitive core of embodied household agents, yet the plans they emit are rarely checked against a grounded model of the environment before execution, and the task-success they report is often measured on benchmarks so saturated that no method can be separated from another.

We present SAGE (Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing), a single-LLM planner built from two lightweight mechanisms: a domain-agnostic symbolic gate (~250 lines of Python, zero tokens, $O(|\pi|)$) that blocks precondition-violating actions with typed reasons as a runtime safety monitor, and a local edit that regenerates only the failed sub-goal's suffix, keeping completed and untouched work intact; a hybrid seed+live memory store supports cold-start coverage.

We evaluate under a leak-free protocol (leave-one-out retrieval) over five open-weight models and a 75-task AI2-THOR benchmark. On the standard benchmark goal-completeness saturates (52% of instances trivially solved) and SAGE ties strong hierarchical baselines.

On a harder, method-agnostic multi-goal composition, SAGE's completeness lead re-emerges large (+0.06 to +0.23 across four models).Under injected mid-execution failures, SAGE recovers as reliably as whole-plan replanners at 2.4-3.3x fewer LLM calls.

As a verify-before-execute gate, the symbolic monitor blocks unsafe actions before actuation and raises simulator-reported step-success for every planner tested (up to +0.11), a signal the verifier never sees (non-circular).

Because the gate calls no model (0.008 ms/plan), it is a safety layer that runs essentially free on the edge: SAGE planning reproduces its quality on a Jetson AGX Orin, where small-model verification helps most.

We release the benchmark, the leak-free protocol, the recovery and safety-gate harnesses, and a verifier-portability study (auto-induced on ALFWorld, 0.89 held-out).

summary.en: The paper presents SAGE, a single-LLM planner combining a symbolic action gate with local suffix editing and hybrid memory for cold-start coverage. The gate blocks actions that violate preconditions before execution, while editing regenerates only the failed sub-goal's remaining plan. Across five open-weight models and 75 AI2-THOR tasks, the saturated standard benchmark does not distinguish methods, and SAGE ties strong hierarchical baselines; it leads on multi-goal composition. Under injected failures, recovery matches whole-plan replanners with fewer calls. The authors also report higher simulator step-success for all tested planners and reproduced planning quality on Jetson AGX Orin.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SAGE，一种用于具身任务规划的单 LLM 系统，结合符号动作门控与局部后缀编辑，并使用混合记忆支持冷启动。符号门在执行前拦截违反前置条件的动作，局部编辑只重新生成失败子目标的后续计划。作者在五种开放权重模型和 75 项 AI2-THOR 任务上评估：标准基准因目标完成度饱和而难以区分方法，SAGE 与强层级基线持平；在多目标组合任务中，其完成度领先。在注入执行中故障时，恢复效果与整计划重规划相当而调用更少。仿真器报告的单步成功率对所有受测规划器均有提升，作者还报告 Jetson AGX Orin 上可复现规划质量。

items.title: SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners

sections.text:
Pretrained robot manipulation policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) or world-action models (WAMs) leave interaction-relevant metric geometry implicit. Recent breakthroughs in spatial reconstruction can supply the necessary geometry reliably, but their features describe local shape without stating where it lies with respect to the robot.

How best to deliver these features to a pretrained policy remains unresolved. We propose Spatial Grafting, a versatile, lightweight spatial module that binds frozen reconstruction features to metric, robot-relative geometry.

Spatial Grafting constructs metric-grounded spatial tokens and injects them into the flow-matching action expert through cross-attention, without modifying the host's perceptual pathway, so the host retains the full benefit of its pretraining.

We evaluate it more broadly than any geometry-aware policy we compare against: one graft architecture, with no per-host redesign, on two VLAs and two WAMs, across four simulation benchmarks that span short-horizon manipulation, visual robustness, clutter and long-horizon mobile manipulation, and on three real-robot platforms with single- and dual-arm configurations.

On RoboTwin 2.0, a dual-arm manipulation benchmark, the graft improves every host across VLAs and WAMs. Grafted $\pi_{0.5}$ gains 11.3% and 15.6% on clean and randomized scenes, reaching 94.0% and 92.4%, above the strongest published 3D-conditioned policy, WAM4D (93.8% and 89.9%).

The margin widens as the horizon lengthens: on tasks from BEHAVIOR-1K, a dual-arm mobile manipulation challenge scored by average task progress, it surpasses the 2025 challenge winner on five of six tasks,by up to 0.47 Q-score, and exceeds a map-conditioned spatial policy on average across the three tasks both report.

summary.en: The paper introduces Spatial Grafting, which binds frozen 3D reconstruction features to metric, robot-relative geometry and injects spatial tokens into a flow-matching action expert through cross-attention. It leaves the pretrained host's perception pathway unchanged. The authors evaluate one graft architecture on two vision-language-action policies and two world-action models, across four simulation benchmarks and three real-robot platforms. On RoboTwin 2.0, it improves every tested host; grafted π0.5 exceeds the cited strongest published 3D-conditioned policy in clean and randomized scenes. On BEHAVIOR-1K, it surpasses the 2025 challenge winner on five of six tasks and beats a map-conditioned policy on average across three shared tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Spatial Grafting，将冻结的空间重建特征与以机器人为参照的度量几何绑定，构造空间 token，并通过交叉注意力注入流匹配动作专家，不改动预训练策略的感知路径。作者以同一架构评估两种视觉语言动作策略和两种世界动作模型，覆盖四个仿真基准及三种真实机器人平台。在 RoboTwin 2.0 双臂操作基准上，该方法提升了所有受测策略；嫁接后的 π0.5 在干净与随机场景中的成绩高于文中所述最强已发表三维条件策略。在 BEHAVIOR-1K 任务中，作者报告其在六项任务中的五项超过 2025 年挑战赛冠军，并在共同报告的三项任务上平均优于地图条件空间策略。

items.title: Spatial Grafting: Grounding 3D Features for Flow-Matching Robot Policies

sections.text:
Driving decisions depend on both where to focus and how to act on what is seen. Effective driving reasoning must establish which objects matter, where they are, and how they inform the intended action. Text-based rationales can describe a driving response while leaving its correspondence to specific visual evidence implicit.

Visual focus provides a concrete starting point for this connection by identifying what matters in the scene and where it is. We propose FocusDrive, a structured multimodal reasoning framework that organizes end-to-end planning around explicit visual focus.

It pairs descriptions of decision-relevant objects with image-patch references, bringing explicit visual focus into the reasoning that generates driving plans and trajectories.

We first assess this focus representation through driver gaze prediction, then investigate its role in planning reasoning using driving-focus annotations within existing NAVSIM training scenes. Experiments on W3DA and NAVSIM demonstrate competitive gaze prediction and end-to-end planning performance, with FocusDrive improving over text-based chain-of-thought.

These results support visual focus as an effective link between scene understanding and driving action.

summary.en: The paper proposes FocusDrive, a multimodal reasoning framework that organizes end-to-end driving planning around explicit visual focus. It pairs descriptions of decision-relevant objects with image-patch references, linking reasoning about plans and trajectories to specific visual evidence. The authors first assess the representation through driver-gaze prediction, then study its role in planning with driving-focus annotations in existing NAVSIM training scenes. Experiments on W3DA and NAVSIM show competitive gaze prediction and end-to-end planning, with improvements over text-based chain-of-thought. The authors conclude that visual focus can effectively connect scene understanding with driving action.
summary.zh: 论文提出 FocusDrive，一种以显式视觉焦点组织端到端驾驶规划的多模态推理框架。它将与决策相关的物体描述和图像块引用配对，使驾驶计划与轨迹推理能够指向具体视觉证据。作者先用驾驶员注视预测评估焦点表征，再利用现有 NAVSIM 训练场景中的驾驶焦点标注研究其规划作用。在 W3DA 和 NAVSIM 上的实验显示，该方法取得有竞争力的注视预测和端到端规划表现，并优于基于文本的思维链。作者据此认为视觉焦点可有效连接场景理解与驾驶动作。

items.title: FocusDrive: Reasoning with Visual Focus for Autonomous Driving

In this work, we present a low-cost, easy-to-make, adaptable, and compact fingertip design for robotic hands that integrates multi-modal tactile sensors. We use strain gauge sensors to capture static forces and a contact microphone sensor to measure

sections.text:
Tactile sensing is critical for enhancing manipulation precision and versatility, but its adoption in robotic hands remains limited due to high sensor costs, manufacturing and integration challenges, and difficulties in extracting expressive and reliable contact information.

In this work, we present a low-cost, easy-to-make, adaptable, and compact fingertip design for robotic hands that integrates multi-modal tactile sensors. We use strain gauge sensors to capture static forces and a contact microphone sensor to measure high-frequency vibrations during contact.

These tactile sensors are integrated into a compact design with a minimal sensor footprint. From sensor characterization, we show that strain gauge sensors provide repeatable 3D force measurements in the 0-5~N range and the contact microphone sensor can captures distinct vibrotactile signatures associated with different material types.

We evaluate our design with three types of manipulation tasks, including slip-aware closed-loop grasping to handle a wide range of objects, cup counting and unstacking with precise contact localization, and box selection and opening with hidden material identification.

Given the expressiveness and reliability of tactile sensor readings, we show that different tactile sensing modalities can be used flexibly in manipulation, solely or together to achieve improved task performance. The design will be open-sourced on the project website: https://sites.google.com/view/tactilefingertip.

summary.en: The paper presents a low-cost, compact, adaptable fingertip design for robotic hands that integrates strain gauges for static forces and a contact microphone for high-frequency vibrations. Sensor characterization indicates repeatable 3D force measurements from the strain gauges over 0–5 N, while the microphone captures distinct vibration signatures associated with material types. The design is evaluated in slip-aware closed-loop grasping, cup counting and unstacking with contact localization, and box selection and opening involving hidden-material identification. The authors state that tactile modalities can be used alone or together to improve task performance.
summary.zh: 论文介绍一种低成本、紧凑且易于制作和适配的机器人手指尖端设计，集成多模态触觉传感器。应变片测量静态力，接触麦克风记录接触时的高频振动。传感器表征显示，应变片可在 0–5 N 范围内重复测量三维力，麦克风则能捕捉与不同材料相关的振动特征。作者在三类操作任务中评估设计：考虑滑移的闭环抓取、杯子计数与拆叠，以及依靠隐藏材料识别的盒子选择和开启。论文称触觉读数具有表达力和可靠性，不同模态可单独或组合用于操作并改善任务表现。

items.title: A multi-modal tactile fingertip design for robotic hands to enhance dexterous manipulation

sections.text:
Scale-consistent ego-motion estimation is fundamental for autonomous ground robots. Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) representation naturally addresses the scale drift problem of monocular visual odometry (MVO) by providing a metric-scaled planar workspace, enabling the simplification of 6-DoF ego-motion to a more robust 3-DoF model.

However, existing BEV-based methods suffer from two key limitations: sparse supervision signals from pose-only training, and information loss during perspective-to-BEV projection. We present BEV-ODOM2, an enhanced framework in the BEV-ODOM line that addresses both limitations without supervision modalities beyond the pose ground truth.

Our approach introduces （1） pose-derived dense rigid BEV flow supervision, which reparameterizes the 3-DoF pose ground truth into a pixel-level training signal, and （2） Perspective View (PV)-BEV fusion, which computes correlation volumes before projection to retain additional motion cues and help alleviate projection ambiguity.

An enhanced rotation sampling strategy further balances diverse motion patterns during training. We evaluate on four datasets with varied spatial scales: KITTI, Oxford, NCLT, and our newly collected ZJH-VO benchmark. BEV-ODOM2 reduces the RTE of BEV-ODOM by 39% on average across the four datasets.

It further enables closed-loop navigation on a physical robot with centimeter-level cross-track error. Real-time inference on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin confirms edge deployment feasibility. The code and the ZJH-VO dataset are publicly released to facilitate future research.

summary.en: The paper presents BEV-ODOM2, a monocular visual odometry framework for ground robots. It derives dense rigid BEV flow supervision from pose ground truth and fuses perspective-view and BEV features before projection to preserve motion cues and reduce projection ambiguity. An enhanced rotation sampling strategy is also used during training. The authors report an average 39% reduction in relative translation error compared with BEV-ODOM across KITTI, Oxford, NCLT, and ZJH-VO. They also report closed-loop navigation on a physical robot and real-time inference on a Jetson AGX Orin.
summary.zh: 论文提出 BEV-ODOM2，用于地面机器人的单目视觉里程计。方法以位姿真值生成稠密刚性 BEV 光流监督，并在投影前融合透视视图与 BEV 特征，以保留运动线索、缓解投影歧义；训练中还采用旋转采样策略。作者称，该方法在 KITTI、Oxford、NCLT 和 ZJH-VO 四个数据集上的相对平移误差较 BEV-ODOM 平均降低 39%。论文还报告了实体机器人闭环导航和 Jetson AGX Orin 实时推理结果。

items.title: BEV-ODOM2: Enhanced BEV-based Monocular Visual Odometry with PV-BEV Fusion and Dense Flow Supervision for Ground Robots

Since graspable locations on these interfaces are spatially limited and discretely distributed, motion planning for MLIVRs

sections.text:
Robot-aided operations in space stations are essential for reducing the workload of astronauts and improving the efficiency of on-orbit activities.

Multi-limbed intra-vehicular robots (MLIVRs) equipped with grappling end-effectors have emerged as a promising solution, as they can securely grasp pre-existing interfaces, such as handrails and seat tracks, thereby enabling stable locomotion and forceful manipulation in microgravity environments.

Since graspable locations on these interfaces are spatially limited and discretely distributed, motion planning for MLIVRs must be addressed jointly with foothold planning. This paper presents a simultaneous path and foothold planning framework based on graph theory for MLIVRs.

The proposed method efficiently searches for feasible stance sequences for a multi-limbed robot while satisfying manipulability constraints.

The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated through simulations in a 3D model of the International Space Station (ISS) cabin, demonstrating its capability to generate feasible and efficient locomotion plans in realistic intra-vehicular environments.

summary.en: The paper proposes a graph-based framework for simultaneous path and foothold planning for multi-limbed robots operating inside space stations. Because graspable interfaces such as handrails and seat tracks provide spatially limited, discrete locations, the planner jointly considers robot paths and limb footholds. It searches for feasible stance sequences subject to manipulability constraints. The authors validate the framework in simulations using a three-dimensional model of an International Space Station cabin, where it generates feasible and efficient locomotion plans. The reported validation is in simulation.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种基于图论的同步路径与落脚点规划框架，面向在空间站舱内活动的多肢机器人。由于扶手和座椅导轨等可抓握位置有限且离散，规划需要联合考虑机器人路径和各肢体的支撑位置。该方法搜索满足可操作性约束的可行姿态序列。作者在国际空间站舱段的三维模型中进行仿真，结果显示框架能够生成可行且高效的舱内移动计划；文中验证范围为仿真环境。

items.title: Graph-Based Simultaneous Path and Foothold Planning for Multi-Limbed Intra-Vehicular Robots in Space Stations

items.intro: arXiv:2511.09484v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Learning agile robotic policies requires large-scale demonstrations, but translating abundant human motion data to robots is bottlenecked by the embodiment gap and missing dynamic information. To bridge this gap, we propose Scalable Physics-Informed DExterous Retargeting (SPIDER), a physics-based retargeting framework to transform and augment kinematic-only human demonstrations into dynamically feasible robot trajectories at scale. Our key insight is that human demonstrations should provide global task structure and objective, while a sampling-based solver can

sections.text:
Learning agile robotic policies requires large-scale demonstrations, but translating abundant human motion data to robots is bottlenecked by the embodiment gap and missing dynamic information.

To bridge this gap, we propose Scalable Physics-Informed DExterous Retargeting (SPIDER), a physics-based retargeting framework to transform and augment kinematic-only human demonstrations into dynamically feasible robot trajectories at scale.

Our key insight is that human demonstrations should provide global task structure and objective, while a sampling-based solver can be used to find the feasible solution given the physics constraints.

As a general framework, SPIDER is an efficient physics-based retargeting method that can be applied to both humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation and dexterous manipulation across 9 humanoid/dexterous hand embodiments, 6 datasets and 3 simulators.

By bypassing the need for policy optimization, it achieves state-of-the-art performance while being 10x faster than reinforcement learning (RL) baselines. Furthermore, SPIDER enables physics-based data augmentation, such as imposing external payloads, perturbations, and new contact patterns, to generate diverse data.

We demonstrate that the retargeted motion can be executed on the robot directly open-loop or serve as feasible reference motion for efficient RL policy learning.

Our pipeline enables large-scale generation of robot trajectories from human motion, and we release a dataset of 6,520 simulated demonstrations across four hands and 191 dataset-specific object identities to support future research.

summary.en: The paper introduces SPIDER, a physics-based framework that retargets and augments kinematic human demonstrations into robot trajectories feasible under dynamics constraints. Demonstrations provide task structure and objectives, while a sampling-based solver searches for feasible solutions. The authors report applications to humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation and dexterous manipulation across multiple embodiments, datasets, and simulators, and state that SPIDER is ten times faster than reinforcement learning baselines. Retargeted motions can be executed open-loop on a robot or used as references for policy learning. The paper also releases a dataset of simulated demonstrations.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SPIDER，一种物理驱动的灵巧动作重定向框架，将仅含运动学信息的人类示范转换并扩增为满足动力学约束的机器人轨迹。其思路是由示范提供任务结构和目标，再用基于采样的求解器寻找可行解。作者称，该方法可用于多种人形机器人全身移动操作和灵巧操作，并在多种具身、数据集及仿真器上评估；相较强化学习基线速度快十倍。论文还报告了仿真示范数据集，并称重定向动作可直接开环执行或作为强化学习参考动作。

items.title: SPIDER: Scalable Physics-Informed Dexterous Retargeting

In contrast, we focus on an under-researched class of high-risk, high-precision motion control problems where actions carry irreversible outcomes, driving sharp peaks and ridges to plague the state-action reward landscape. Using computational pool as a representative example of such problems

sections.text:
Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms for movement control are typically evaluated and benchmarked on sequential decision tasks where imprecise actions may be corrected with later actions, thus allowing high returns with noisy actions.

In contrast, we focus on an under-researched class of high-risk, high-precision motion control problems where actions carry irreversible outcomes, driving sharp peaks and ridges to plague the state-action reward landscape.

Using computational pool as a representative example of such problems, we propose and evaluate State-Conditioned Shooting (SCOOT), a novel DRL algorithm that builds on advantage-weighted regression (AWR) with three key modifications: 1) Performing policy optimization only using elite samples, allowing the policy to better latch on to the rare high-reward action samples; 2) Utilizing a mixture-of-experts (MoE) policy, to allow switching between reward landscape modes depending on the state; 3) Adding a distance regularization term and a learning curriculum to encourage exploring diverse strategies before adapting to the most advantageous samples.

We showcase our features' performance in learning physically-based billiard shots demonstrating high action precision and discovering multiple shot strategies for a given ball configuration.

summary.en: The paper studies high-risk, high-precision motion control, where actions can have irreversible outcomes and the reward landscape contains sharp peaks and ridges. Using computational pool as an example, the authors propose State-Conditioned Shooting (SCOOT), a deep reinforcement learning algorithm based on advantage-weighted regression. It optimizes using elite samples, uses a mixture-of-experts policy for state-dependent reward modes, and adds distance regularization and a learning curriculum to encourage diverse exploration before adapting to advantageous samples. The authors demonstrate precise billiard shots and the discovery of multiple strategies for a given configuration.
summary.zh: 论文研究高风险、高精度运动控制问题，其中动作可能造成不可逆结果，奖励景观因此呈现尖峰和脊线。作者以计算机桌球为例，提出 State-Conditioned Shooting（SCOOT），一种基于优势加权回归的深度强化学习算法。其设计包括仅用精英样本优化策略、采用混合专家策略以适应不同状态下的奖励模式，以及加入距离正则项和学习课程，先鼓励多样探索，再适应高回报样本。作者展示了物理桌球击球任务中的高精度控制及多种策略发现。

items.title: Learning High-Risk High-Precision Motion Control

sections.text:
While Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform strongly on manipulation tasks, their responses to invalid task premises remain underexplored. Existing evaluations of premise conflicts often focus on terminal task outcomes, yet task failure alone cannot distinguish behavioral disengagement from continued pursuit followed by an execution error.

We call the latter pattern Failed Persistence. To study this phenomenon, we introduce ConflictVLA-Bench, which pairs conflict rollouts with premise-consistent reference rollouts and evaluates both outcomes and execution processes.

Built on LIBERO, the benchmark contains 2,826 prompt-conditioned conflict tasks spanning four conflict families, four structural configurations, and two prompt conditions. Across all eight VLAs, invalid premises reduce original goal completion by at least 17.3 percentage points, with the reduction reaching 56.2 percentage points for OpenVLA.

Crucially, even when models succeed on premise-consistent tasks and fail on their matched conflict tasks, they often continue to approach the original targets, retain early trajectory structure, and show limited action magnitude suppression. Failed Persistence therefore recurs across the evaluated models.

Explicit premise checking does not consistently produce selective and coordinated behavioral changes. These findings show that terminal failure alone establishes neither behavioral disengagement nor refusal and that outcomes alone are insufficient for VLA evaluation.

Experimental data and additional details are available on the project page: https://github.com/EmbodiedAISurvey/ConflictVLA-Bench

summary.en: The paper introduces ConflictVLA-Bench to evaluate both outcomes and execution processes when vision-language-action models encounter invalid task premises. Built on LIBERO, the benchmark covers four conflict families, four structural configurations, and two prompt conditions. The authors report reduced goal completion across all eight evaluated models and recurring Failed Persistence: models often continue approaching original targets, retain early trajectory structure, and suppress action magnitude only modestly. Explicit premise checking does not consistently produce selective, coordinated behavioral changes. The authors argue that terminal failure alone cannot establish disengagement or refusal.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ConflictVLA-Bench，用于评估视觉-语言-动作模型面对无效任务前提时的行为过程与任务结果。基准基于 LIBERO，涵盖四类冲突、四种结构配置和两种提示条件。作者报告，八种模型在冲突任务上的目标完成率均下降，并反复出现“失败后仍持续执行”现象：模型继续接近原目标、保留早期轨迹结构，动作幅度抑制有限。显式检查前提未能稳定带来有选择且协调的行为变化；作者指出，仅凭任务失败不足以判断模型是否停止行动或拒绝执行。

items.title: ConflictVLA-Bench: Benchmarking Behavioral Responses of Vision-Language-Action Models to Premise Conflicts

sections.text:
Adapting a pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model to a new robot, environment, or task requires demonstrations that are collected locally and often discarded. Federated learning is a promising approach to exploiting such distributed demonstrations by learning a shared policy.

However, whether it can adapt large pretrained VLAs remains an open question, and a lack of reproducible benchmarks for pretrained VLAs and reusable training frameworks makes existing results difficult to compare.

In this paper, we conduct a systematic study of federated fine-tuning of three modern pretrained VLA policies on the 40 simulated tasks of the LIBERO manipulation benchmark, and on six real-world tasks in two real-robot experiments, with demonstrations collected across two and three sites, respectively.

Our study analyzes the key choices in this setting, spanning multiple federated parameter scopes, three aggregation algorithms, and evaluation under distribution shift.

Based on the study, we derive a series of lessons, including the dominance of the federated scope over the choice of aggregation algorithm and the difficulty of matching centralized fine-tuning on physical robots, where cross-site heterogeneity is stronger than simulation captures.

We also highlight opportunities for federated VLA learning, such as the ability to match centralized fine-tuning on heterogeneous data, to remain at least as robust as centralized fine-tuning under distribution shift, and to personalize, with each client federating part of the policy and keeping the rest local, which helps where the policy's pretraining is weak but leaves no usable global model.

We open-source \decentvla{}, the model- and runtime-agnostic testbed behind the study, to facilitate future research and fair comparisons in federated VLA learning.

summary.en: The paper studies federated fine-tuning for pretrained vision-language-action policies through simulated LIBERO tasks and two real-robot experiments. It examines federated parameter scopes, aggregation algorithms, and distribution shift. The authors conclude that the federated scope matters more than the aggregation algorithm, and that matching centralized fine-tuning is difficult on physical robots because cross-site heterogeneity is stronger than simulation captures. They also identify opportunities involving heterogeneous data, robustness under distribution shift, and personalization, and release a model- and runtime-agnostic testbed to support future research and comparisons.
summary.zh: 论文系统研究预训练视觉-语言-动作策略的联邦微调，评估涵盖 LIBERO 中的模拟任务及两项真实机器人实验，并分析联邦参数范围、聚合算法和分布偏移。作者总结，联邦参数范围对结果的影响超过聚合算法选择；在真实机器人上，由于跨站点异质性强于模拟所体现的程度，联邦微调难以达到集中式微调表现。论文还讨论异质数据、分布偏移鲁棒性和个性化方面的机会，并发布模型与运行时无关的测试平台，以支持后续研究和比较。

items.title: An Empirical Study and Open Testbed for Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language-Action Models
